description.narrative:
Nexus Consortium Somalia represents a coalition of ten local and national NGOs committed to advancing locally-led humanitarian, development, and peacebuilding solutions in Somalia. Recent reductions in USAID humanitarian funding have severely impacted the operational capacity of Nexus members, threatening the progress made toward localization and resilience building. To sustain critical coordination, advocacy, and capacity-building efforts, there is an urgent need for strategic institutional support. Nexus seeks seed funding to reinforce its operational backbone, enabling it to lead key localization advocacy initiatives, maintain essential personnel, and engage in global-local dialogues aimed at shaping more equitable humanitarian action.
Objectives: •Sustain Nexus Secretariat operations to coordinate and support member organizations during a period of financial uncertainty. •Strengthen advocacy and representation of Somali civil society in regional and international localization, humanitarian financing, and policy forums. •Build the internal capacity of Nexus Secretariat to mobilize resources and scale impact-driven programming in humanitarian innovation, green response, and protection. Key Activities (June 2025–May 2026): •Partial salary support for essential Secretariat staff: Executive Director, Finance Officer, Program Support Officer, and Business Development Officer. •Office operational support (utilities, internet, communications, supplies). •Participation of the Executive Director and Secretariat representatives in advocacy and localization workshops, meetings, and policy dialogues. •Engagement with potential donors and humanitarian partners through networking events and strategic missions. •Hosting two in-country roundtable discussions with local CSOs and international partners on localization and sustainable humanitarian financing. •Conducting statutory Audits
Expected Outcomes: •Sustained operational continuity for the Nexus Secretariat. •Strengthened presence and voice of Somali civil society in global and regional humanitarian dialogues. •Increased access to funding opportunities for Nexus members through strategic partnerships and donor engagement. •Enhanced internal capacity to manage, implement, and scale innovative localization initiatives.

participating-org.narrative:
Nexus is a unique consortium, led by eight pioneering Somali NGOs, aspiring to advance a locally driven agenda for change by building partnerships between communities, civil society and the public and private sectors as well as through the implementationof integrated and sustainable interventions across the triple nexus of humanitarian, peace and development.
Founded in 2019, Nexus is a paradigm-shifting platform comprising of Eight core members: • Centre for Peace and Democracy (CPD) • Gargaar Relief and Development Organization (GREDO) • Horn of Africa Voluntary Youth Committee (HAVOYOCCO) • KAALO • Save Somali Women and Children (SSWC) • Social-Life and Agriculture Development Organization (SADO) • Taakulo Somaliland Community (TASCO) • Wajir South Development Association (WASDA)
The eight NEXUS member organizations bring to the table rich and incredibly diverse strengths and qualities that makes the platform stronger and grow exponentially going forward. Their extensive expertise and experience across varying thematic areas, and their relationships and rapport amongst one other is the most significant qualities that enriches the platform to achieve its strategic objectives. The organizations’ presence in all the regions in Somalia/Somaliland and their decades of involvement in humanitarian interventions make them a strong force in Somalia’s ever evolving and highly competitive humanitarian space.
Nexus core members possess wide-ranging technical capacities and represent communitiesacross all Federal Member States of Somalia and Somaliland. Nexus alsohas two international partners who are committed to the localization agenda – Oxfam and Save the Children
The members have been implementing humanitarian, development and conflict prevention, mitigation and response programs amidst relative calm, conflict and during disasters (both natural and man-made). It is the experience that gives the members the confidence and agility to continue working for such a long time. Nexus’ approach isambitious but is grounded in the widely recognized need for more dynamic interventions tothe chronic challenges faced by Somalia and Somaliland.
